segments.text: Bulls hate the color red. Well, that's not exactly true. They can't even see it properly.
Cattle are red-green colorblind. To a bull, a red cape looks dull, kind of a muddy gray.
Here's the wild part. What makes a bull charge is the movement. The matador whips the cape around, and the bull goes after whatever is moving.
Tests showed it: bulls charged a waving blue or white cloth just as hard as a red one, and ignored a red cape that stayed still.
So why red? Mostly tradition, and it hides the blood.
So bulls don't hate red. They hate being waved at. Honestly, same.
